title: Security of the Nonce-and-Counter Tweak Mode
summary: The nonce-and-counter tweak mode is conjectured to offer beyond-birthday-bound security with respected nonces and robustness under nonce misuse; proving or refuting both guarantees remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether the authenticated-encryption mode for a tweakable block cipher that concatenates the nonce and block counter in the tweak input and uses the IV as the plaintext input achieves beyond-birthday-bound security under nonce-respecting use and robust security under nonce misuse; either prove these guarantees or provide a counterexample. Account for the mode's drawback that it requires a larger, and therefore costly, tweak length.

scope.domain: Authenticated-encryption modes for tweakable block ciphers using a nonce-and-counter tweak.
assumptions: Nonce-respecting use for the beyond-birthday-bound security objective
Nonce misuse for the robust-security objective
parameters: Nonce and block counter — concatenated to form the tweak input
IV — used as the plaintext input
Tweak length — enlarged by the construction and identified as costly
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove that the mode meets both stated security objectives or provide a counterexample, while accounting for the cost of the larger tweak length.

citations.label: Counter-in-Tweak: Authenticated Encryption Modes for Tweakable Block Ciphers

progress.summary: The source presents the mode's security as an explicit conjecture rather than an established result and highlights the costly larger tweak length as an important drawback.
citation_labels: Thomas Peyrin et al., Counter-in-Tweak: Authenticated Encryption Modes for Tweakable Block Ciphers
